_meta.source: github REST API + repo pages, fetched live during this run

fields.capture: auto = software observes you; manual = you press start/stop; derived = another tool feeds it
fields.android: what actually runs on a phone, not what the README aspires to
fields.verdict: why it is or is not the thing asked for: ActivityWatch, mine, cross phone+linux

projects.name: ActivityWatch
projects.linux: aw-watcher-window (X11 good, Wayland patchy), aw-watcher-afk (X11 only in practice)
projects.android: aw-android, Kotlin, bundles aw-server-rust locally; UsageStats based
projects.cross_device: weak: each device holds its own server; aw-sync is file-sync based and Android is not part of it
projects.verdict: the reference design and the right data model. Its actual gap is exactly the one asked about.

projects.name: aw-server-rust
projects.cross_device: single-instance; sync is out of scope
projects.verdict: drop-in alternative to the kuhytrack server if you want Rust instead of 600 lines of Python. Same API.

projects.name: aw-android
projects.api: exposes the standard REST API on the phone's loopback
projects.cross_device: no push to a remote server
projects.verdict: keep it installed even if you build your own: it is the only no-root legal source of foreground-app data, and Termux can read its loopback API. That is the kt-bridge-awandroid.sh path.

projects.name: beaverhabits
projects.api: limited; storage is per-user JSON-ish records
projects.cross_device: yes, trivially — it is one server and a browser
projects.verdict: different product. Answers 'did I do the thing' not 'where did my hours go'. Its cross-device story works precisely because it never touches the OS.

projects.name: focus_flow_cloud
projects.verdict: 43 stars, one author, no LICENSE file — using it means adopting it. Its session concept is worth 30 lines in your own schema, not a dependency.

projects.name: OpenHabitTracker
projects.verdict: the best-executed cross-platform story of the list, but it is .NET/MAUI. On Arch that is a toolchain you would maintain forever for a habit checkbox.

projects.name: solidtime
projects.verdict: built for invoicing clients and teams. You are not billing anyone. Heaviest stack on the list for the least relevant feature set.

projects.name: timetagger
projects.api: REST with a sync-friendly record model
projects.cross_device: yes — its sync model is genuinely good
projects.verdict: the cleanest self-hostable manual tracker, and its offline-first record sync is worth reading. But it will never tell you what you did without you telling it.

projects.name: traggo
projects.verdict: single binary + sqlite is the right deployment shape, and the tag model beats project/task hierarchies. Still manual. GraphQL for this is overkill.

projects.name: wakapi
projects.cross_device: yes — every editor pushes to one server
projects.verdict: the only other auto-capture tool here, and it already solves the multi-device problem the right way (dumb clients, one server). Run it alongside; import it with kt-import.py wakapi. It cannot see anything outside your editor.

projects.name: Ziit
projects.verdict: a younger, prettier wakapi with 18x fewer stars and a heavier runtime. If you want editor stats, wakapi is the lower-risk pick.
